title: Affine proper squares and global stratified module refinement
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For each $k$-scheme $Z$ put $A_Z=p_Z^*\underline\Omega$ on its small pro-etale site, with the finite-subextension condensed convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed; sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal $A_Z$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the exact coefficient-cartesian inverse images of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients].

Let $T$ be of finite type over $k$, $p:P\to T$ proper, and $h:T'\hookrightarrow T$ a quasi-compact locally closed immersion, meaning a composite of a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $T$ and that open inclusion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-weil-proper-morphism; def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $P'=P\times_TT'$. Let $N$ be an internal $A_P$-module such that Zariski locally on $P$ there is a finite partition by locally closed subschemes on each of which the inverse image of $N$ is pro-etale locally free of finite rank. No absolute separatedness of $T$ or $P$ is assumed.

For every affine open subscheme $U\subseteq T$, put $P_U=P\times_TU$, $T'_U=T'\times_TU$ and $P'_U=P'\times_TU$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $U,T'_U,P_U,P'_U$ are separated and of finite type over $k$, hence satisfy the standing scheme hypotheses [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]; both $p_U:P_U\to U$ and $p'_U:P'_U\to T'_U$ are proper. The scheme $P_U$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth; def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and is quasi-separated.

For every finite affine open cover $W_a$ of $P_U$ subordinate to the given local stratifications, there is a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification $s_b:S_b\to P_U$ such that each $s_b$ factors by an actual scheme morphism through a stratum of one of the restricted stratifications on $W_a$. On every $S_b$, the inverse image $s_b^*(N|_{P_U})$ is pro-etale locally free of finite rank, hence locally finitely presented. Here constructible means that the image is a finite union of locally closed subsets with quasi-compact open parts, and an immersed stratification means disjoint images covering $P_U$ [def-constructible-stratification]. Consequently $(N|_{P_U})[0]$ belongs to the full ordinary bounded constructible derived category $D_{\mathrm{cons}}((P_U)_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{P_U})$ of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Rank zero, varying finite ranks and empty strata or schemes are allowed.

For the module condition: Bhatt--Scholze Definitions 6.8.3, 6.8.6 and 6.8.8, with the existing qcqs local-gluing-core node. Agent expansion of returned proof steps 6--7.

proof.text: The open immersion $U\to T$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2). Its composite with $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Since $U$ is affine, its structure map to the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact, so it is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. This establishes the two required properties of $U$ without separatedness of $T$.

The quasi-compact immersion $h$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2), hence of finite type by definition. Thus $h_U:T'_U\to U$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2), and is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](1). It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](a). By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), $p_U$ and $p'_U$ are proper: both are base changes of $p$, the latter along $T'_U\to T$. Proper maps are separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Compose the structure maps along $T'_U\to U$, $P_U\to U$, and $P'_U\to T'_U$. Composition of finite-type maps [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) and of separated maps [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) gives all remaining corner assertions. Therefore all four corners satisfy [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting].

The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$; $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point, so is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $P_U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It gives that $P_U$ is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], it is also quasi-separated. In particular the qcqs hypothesis of the local-gluing theorem is satisfied.

Fix the given finite affine cover $W_a$ subordinate to the local stratifications. A restricted local stratum is the fibre product of its original immersion with $W_a\to P$, not an arbitrary subscheme having the same underlying image; it is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](1). Pullback preserves the stated finite-free local trivializations as follows. On a trivializing pro-etale cover, a free module $R^r$ has presentation $\operatorname{coker}(0:R^0\to R^r)$ [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. For a local stratum $\iota:Z\to V\subseteq P$, put $T_{a,c}=Z\times_PW_a$ with projection $f:T_{a,c}\to Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-local-finite-presentation-inverse-image] with $m_i=0,n_i=r_i$ to $f$ and the module $\iota^*N$: it supplies the base-changed covering and the same zero-relation presentation, which is again free of rank $r_i$. The coefficient-ring identification is exactly [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1). The composition isomorphism [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp] for the two factorizations $T_{a,c}\to Z\to P$ and $T_{a,c}\to W_a\to P$ identifies $f^*\iota^*N$ with the inverse image of $N$ along the restricted stratum. Thus the restricted local strata still have finite-free restrictions of $N$. Since $P_U$ is of finite type over a field, its topological space is Noetherian as in [def-weil-constructible-subset]; open subspaces inherit the descending-chain condition on closed sets by taking closures. Hence every locally closed local stratum in each $W_a$ is constructible by the same node (Tag 005L). The restricted families therefore meet all hypotheses of the local-gluing theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core] to $X=P_U$ and the restricted stratifications on $W_a$. Obtain a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification $s_b:S_b\to P_U$ and actual factorization morphisms $v_b:S_b\to T_{a,c}$ with $s_b$ equal to the composite of $v_b$ and the local stratum immersion into $P_U$. This uses precisely the morphism-factorization clause of that node, not merely an inclusion of images. The composition comparison [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp] identifies $s_b^*(N|_{P_U})$ with the inverse image by $v_b$ of the local restriction. Apply [lem-sfb-local-finite-presentation-inverse-image] to its zero-relation presentations as in the preceding step. The resulting pro-etale covering of $S_b$ makes the module finite free, and [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) identifies its ring with $A_{S_b}$. This proves the requested module assertion on every global stratum.

source.place: Tag 03S0 (lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), locality reduction; internal-module inverse-image construction and Bhatt--Scholze Definition 6.8.3

proof.text: On each trivializing cover the finite-free restriction has presentation $0\to A_{S_b}^{r}$ with cokernel $A_{S_b}^{r}$: the identity on $A_{S_b}^{r}$ satisfies the cokernel universal property since every map annihilates the zero source. By [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module] and [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented], each stratum restriction is locally finitely presented. The finite immersed stratification from the preceding step now witnesses that $N|_{P_U}$ is constructible by [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Its degree-zero complex has $H^0=N|_{P_U}$ and $H^i=0$ for $i\ne0$, by the kernels and images of its zero differentials. Zero is also constructible on the same strata, using the rank-zero presentation. With bounds $a=b=0$, [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] gives membership in the full ordinary bounded constructible category. All arguments allow $r=0$ and varying $r_i$; for $P_U=\varnothing$ take the empty stratification and the same bounds.
